title: Watch Horsetail Fall glow at sunset
description: On a few evenings in late February, sunset can light the narrow ribbon of Horsetail Fall on El Capitan until it appears to glow orange against the granite. Walk into Yosemite Valley with other hopeful viewers, settle in before dusk, and watch the light shift across the cliff. The effect needs both flowing water and a clear sky, so the anticipation is part of the experience—and a sighting is never guaranteed.
teaser: Wait for a winter waterfall to catch the last light on El Capitan.
goodToKnow: Check the National Park Service’s current Horsetail Fall viewing guidance before traveling. Viewing often involves a walk after dark; bring warm layers and a headlamp. Flowing water, clear weather, and the right sunset angle all have to align.
whyItMightDelightYou: The moment feels rare because nothing is staged: you wait with the valley, watching ordinary granite become briefly luminous.
